Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has widened the exit of the front‑brake ducts, giving the brakes a stronger stream of cooling air. That extra cooling helps keep the brakes from overheating on a demanding circuit, so the drivers can push harder for longer without losing grip. In short, more brake stability means a better chance of fighting at the front of the grid this weekend.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull’s rear‑corner aerodynamics have been tweaked – the in‑board wing has been reshaped to better manage the loads it sees. This gives the car a more stable rear end, especially through high‑speed corners, which should translate into more grip and confidence on the track. The result could be a noticeable boost in cornering speed and consistency over the weekend.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has trimmed the size of one of the front‑wing flaps, shaving off a bit of surface area. This makes the wing a little less “twitchy,” giving the car a smoother airflow up front and improving stability through the slower corners of this weekend’s circuit. In short, the tweak should help the drivers keep the car balanced and extract more grip where it counts most.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls has tweaked the shape of both the front‑ and rear‑brake ducts to better suit this circuit’s cooling demands. The new geometry helps keep the brakes at optimal temperature, so drivers can push harder into the corners without losing grip. In short, better‑cooled brakes mean more consistent braking performance and a stronger chance to fight for positions this weekend.
